Article title: The public's perception of an earthquake early warning system: A study on factors influencing continuance intention. This study seeks to understanding the basic e-Health services continuance usage intention among patients by integrating the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and extending them by including certain external variables. With a well-structured questionnaire, a survey of 453 respondents – out-patients and care-givers, who should have used e-Health services at least once, in particular, visited multispecialty hospitals, revealed that along with the ECM and TAM constructs such as satisfaction, confirmation, perceived ease-of-use, and perceived usefulness, the external variables such as trust, social influence, perceived service quality, and perceived privacy and security had a significant influence (p < 0.05) on e-Health services continuance usage. The main findings of the study contribute to developing and empirically testing a model that explains the basic process of motivating the e-Health service users for continuance usage intention. results.content: Frontiers in Public Health 01 frontiersin.org Research on the influencing factors of users’ continuance intentions of wearable medical devices—a perspective integrating the UTAUT model and gamification elements Yulin Tian 1, Zoumin Li 1, Dong Liu 2* and Sangbum Son 3 1 School of Business, Shandong Xiehe University, Jinan, Shandong, China, 2 School of Business Administration, Shandong Women’s University, Jinan, China, 3 Department of Global Business, Yeungnam University, Gyeongsan, Republic of Korea With the global aging population and the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases, the application of wearable medical devices in health management has garnered widespread attention. This study develops a research framework by combining the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) model with gamification components to methodically examine the critical factors influencing users’ sustained intention to use wearable medical devices (WMD). KEYWORDS wearable medical devices, gamification, UTAUT model, users’ continuous usage intention, structural equation modeling 1 Introduction In recent years, with the intensification of population aging and the trend of diseases occurring at younger ages, the prevalence of chronic diseases has significantly increased, drawing widespread social attention to health issues. OPEN ACCESS EDITED BY Rizwan Raheem Ahmed, Indus University, Pakistan REVIEWED BY Jun-Phil Uhm, Inha University, Republic of Korea Rana Salman Anwar, Indus University, Pakistan *CORRESPONDENCE Dong Liu bruceliu@ RECEIVED 29 March 2025 ACCEPTED 24 June 2025 PUBLISHED 18 July 2025 CITATION Tian Y, Li Z, Liu D and Son S (2025) Research on the influencing factors of users’ continuance intentions of wearable medical devices—a perspective integrating the UTAUT model and gamification elements. To address this research gap, this study will combine the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) model to explore the mechanism by which gamification affects users’ intention to continue using WMD. These factors include PE (users’ perceptions of the effectiveness and practicality of using WMD for health monitoring and management), EE (the time and effort users perceive they need to invest in using WMD), SI (the behavioral expectations users feel from significant others or social groups), and FC (whether users receive adequate technical Tian et al.  10.3389/fpubh.2025.1602230 Frontiers in Public Health 03 frontiersin.org support, device resources, and environmental guarantees when using WMD). Therefore, in the context of this study, integrating gamification with the UTAUT model offers a more comprehensive understanding of users’ continued intention to use medical wearable devices.

results.title: Factors influencing mobile data service (MDS) continuance intention: An empirical study - ScienceDirect
results.content: System service quality, service mobility, and customer experience impact MDS continuance intention. Utilizing an integrated model drawn from the theory of planned behavior and quality frameworks, we examine the impact of both system service quality and service mobility on continuance intention and the mediating effect of customer experience among MDS users. Results indicated that 41.4% of MDS users’ continuance intention is explained by system service quality, service mobility, and customer experience. A key finding of this study is that customer experience, as a decision tool, has a positive relationship with MDS continuance intention, partially mediating the relationship between system service quality, service mobility, and MDS continuance intention. Drawing upon theory of planned behavior and integrating it with a system service quality construct, this present study investigates the factors that affect the customers’ decision of continuing to use mobile data service.

results.title: Mobile apps for healthy living: Factors influencing continuance intention for health apps - ScienceDirect
results.content: Prior research investigates what affects adoption of a health app, but few studies consider Continuance Intention (CI) for mobile health apps. Drawing on the Information Systems Continuance Model and integrating social (i.e. subjective norms) and psychological factors (i.e. flow experience, health consciousness, behavioral change techniques), we develop a framework testing the factors influencing users’ CI for health apps. Considering the economic relevance of health apps and the potentially positive societal and behavioral changes that they may create, this study investigates why users continue to use health apps for developing healthier lifestyles, such as fitness, diet, meditation, and sleep monitoring apps. Recent studies also consider the factors determining the acceptance and intention to use health apps (Chen and Lin, 2018; Okumus et al., 2018; Rohde et al., 2017). However, few studies investigated what motivates users’ continuance intention (CI) for health apps (Beldad and Hegner, 2018; Cho, 2016). Consequently, to explain CI for health apps, we expand the IS Continuance model (Bhattacherjee, 2001), by integrating social (i.e. subjective norms) and psychological factors (i.e. flow, health consciousness, behavior change techniques). With more built-in features such as planning, goal setting, self-monitoring and receiving continuous feedback (Walsh et al., 2016), mobile health apps have become convenient technologically based platforms to incorporate BCTs. BCTs integrated into health apps may substantially increase users’ physical activity, self-image, and health motivation (Dallinga et al., 2015; Walsh et al., 2016). However, the influence of BCT on users’ intentions to continue to use health apps has not been studied previously. The paper, thus, contributes to theory by integrating social (i.e. subjective norms) and psychological factors (i.e. flow experience, health consciousness, behavior change techniques) into the IS Continuance model (Bhattacherjee, 2001). This study develops a theoretical framework, augmenting the IS Continuance model (Bhattacherjee, 2001) by integrating subjective norms as a social factor; and flow experience, BCTs and health consciousness as psychological factors, to explain CI for health apps. ### Expanding the technology acceptance model with the inclusion of trust, social influence, and health valuation to determine the predictors of German users' willingness to continue using a fitness app: a structural equation modeling approach.

results.title: Factors influencing students’ continuance usage intention with online learning during the pandemic: a...
results.content: This study aims to identify the factors affecting students’ satisfaction with online learning, examine the relationship between satisfaction and continuance usage intention, and explore the direct and moderating role of self-quarantine during a pandemic situation. An integrated model is being proposed in this study to measure the continuance usage intention of students adopting e-learning services. This study investigates the impact of these factors on university students' continuance intention to adopt e-learning, exploring the relationships between each determinant. Anchored in the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) framework, this study employed a meta-analytic approach to investigate the effects of seven key antecedents (i.e., Performance Expectation, Effort Expectation, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, Hedonic Motivation, Price Value, and Habit) and possible moderators on Behavioral Intention (BI) towards using e-learning. Anchored in the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) framework, this study employed a meta-analytic approach to investigate the effects of seven key antecedents (i.e., Performance Expectation, Effort Expectation, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, Hedonic Motivation, Price Value, and Habit) and possible moderators on Behavioral Intention (BI) towards using e-learning. (2022) conducted cross-country research to examine the factors affecting students' online learning satisfaction and continuance usage intention during the pandemic. Our study, conducted within the context of an Italian university course, employs the Extended Expectation-Confirmation Model (EECM) as a theoretical framework to explore the key aspects of students’ acceptance and continued intention to use IVR and Metaverse integrated learning environments in educational settings. Based on constructivism theory and the Information System Success Model, this study suggests a research model that examines the factors that influence students' collaborative engagement and satisfaction in an e-learning system setting. Purpose This study examines learner satisfaction and success as mechanisms through which online learning quality translates into learners’ continuous intentions of use by extending DeLone and McLean’s information system success model. This study can provide reference for basic theory and variable selection for subsequent research on the influencing factors of EFL students’ continuance learning intentions in China and elsewhere. The present study is designed to identify the factors influencing the behavioral intention of agricultural students at universities in Iran to use online learning systems in the future.
